class.name: Mesh4D
class.description: Mesh4D is the base class for all 4D meshes. Meshes are used to represent the visuals of objects in 4D space. All 4D meshes have rect bounds, validation, and a proxy mesh for representing the mesh in 3D-based rendering engines. For a wireframe-only mesh, use [WireMesh4D] or one of its descendants. Meshes may also have tetrahedral cells, which are the equivalent of triangles in 3D meshes. For a tetrahedral mesh, use [TetraMesh4D] or one of its descendants. Advanced users can create custom mesh classes by extending the appropriate class.

method.name: _append_proxy_mesh_surfaces_3d
method.description: Callback method that should append surfaces to the given 3D proxy mesh. Do not call this method directly. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method append_proxy_mesh_surfaces_3d] for details.

method.name: _validate_material_for_mesh
method.description: Callback method that should validate a material for a mesh, ensuring that the material is suitable for rendering the mesh. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method validate_material_for_mesh] for details of the input and output.

method.name: _validate_mesh_data
method.description: Callback method that should validate the mesh data. Do not call this method. This can be overridden by derived classes when creating a custom mesh type in GDScript or another scripting language. This method should return [code]true[/code] if the mesh data is valid, and [code]false[/code] if it is not. If the mesh data is invalid, the mesh will be skipped when rendering.

method.name: append_proxy_mesh_surfaces_3d
method.description: Rebuilds the 3D mesh surfaces used to represent this Mesh4D in 3D-based rendering engines, and commit those surfaces to the given 3D proxy mesh. Existing surfaces will be kept. Can be called to commit the current state to a custom proxy mesh, but typically should only be called internally.

method.name: deduplicate_edge_indices
method.description: Static helper method for deduplicating edge indices. This method ensures that each pair of two integers in the array is unique, and that the first index is less than the second index. This is useful for optimizing wireframe meshes by removing duplicate edges and ensuring a consistent order for each edge. [b]Note:[/b] This only looks at edge indices. It does not remove duplicate vertices, nor does it have access to the vertices array.

method.name: get_proxy_mesh_3d
method.description: Returns the proxy 3D mesh that the tetrahedral renderers hand to Godot's own 3D renderer. It stores this mesh's 4D data in its ordinary vertex channels, so it will only render properly with one of the shader materials from [method Material4D.get_cross_section_material_3d] or [method Material4D.get_projected_material_3d], depending on which renderer is in use.

method.name: get_rect_bounds
method.description: Returns the rectangular bounds of the mesh in 4D space. The bounds are represented as a [PackedVector4Array] containing the position and size of the bounding box. The first element is the position (minimum corner) and the second element is the size, where the maximum corner can be calculated as the sum of the position and size. This matches Godot's 3D [AABB] structure.

method.name: is_mesh_data_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the mesh data is valid. This method checks if the data in a mesh is valid for rendering. If the mesh data is invalid, the mesh will be skipped when rendering. This method is called internally by the rendering server, but may also be called manually. If a mesh has valid data, the result of the validation will be cached until the mesh data changes, so this method may be called multiple times without performance concerns. This also means this method should be called after generating a mesh. This especially useful when generating a mesh on a thread; calling this on the thread will avoid stalling the main thread with mesh validation during rendering.

method.name: mark_mesh_bounds_and_proxy_mesh_3d_dirty
method.description: Marks the mesh bounds and the proxy 3D mesh as dirty, meaning they need to be updated. Must be called by subclasses whenever the underlying 4D mesh data changes. This implies [method mark_proxy_mesh_3d_dirty], so there is no need to also call that method when calling this one.

method.name: mark_proxy_mesh_3d_dirty
method.description: Marks the proxy 3D mesh as dirty, meaning it needs to be updated. Must be called by subclasses whenever the underlying 4D mesh data changes.

method.name: reset_mesh_data_validation
method.description: Resets the validation state of the mesh data. This method clears the cached validation state of the mesh data, so that the next call to [method is_mesh_data_valid] will revalidate the mesh data. This is useful when the mesh data has changed and you want to ensure that the mesh is revalidated before rendering. This will be called automatically on built-in types such as [ArrayTetraMesh4D] and [ArrayWireMesh4D] when the mesh data changes.

method.name: validate_material_for_mesh
method.description: Validates that the given material can be used for this mesh. This method may alter the material data if needed to make it compatible with the mesh. For example, if the material has per-edge colors, it will ensure that the color array is at least as big as the amount of edges in the mesh. This method is called automatically when running [method MeshInstance4D.get_active_material], but may also be called manually.

signal.name: mesh_data_validation_reset
signal.description: Emitted when the mesh data's validation is reset and needs to be revalidated. This will happen when any of the mesh's data is modified or cleared. Listeners should NOT immediately call [method is_mesh_data_valid] in response to this signal, because this may be emitted in the middle of a larger editing operation. Instead, this can be used to flag that the mesh needs to be revalidated at a later point. This is especially useful if additional validation is required beyond the automatic checks performed by the mesh itself.
